newsitem.title: UK: N.Electric spurns CE, holds H1 results.
newsitem.headline: N.Electric spurns CE, holds H1 results.

text.p: Britain's Northern Electric, the subject of a hostile takeover bid by CE Electric, a 70 percent-owned unit of U.S. energy group CalEnergy Co Inc, said on Monday it believed the price CE has offered for its shares was too low.

In its first formal defence since CE posted its 630 pence per share bid on November 5, Northern said it would be announcing its interim results by the end of this month, and would also provide shareholders with "important financial information" demonstrating its value.
Northern Electric said in a statement the 630 pence offer price was "below even the lowest price put to Northern Electric by the bidder prior to the launch of its hostile offer."

Northern said when the bid was launched that CE Electric had suggested a price of 700 pence per share, a claim that the U.S. group, which has already bought nearly 30 percent of the regional electricity company (Rec), has denied.

Northern said if the bid lapsed, it would still pay out a second special dividend of 56.5 pence in February 1997, part of a 560 million pound ($934.2 million) package made to fend off Trafalgar House, now part of Kvaerner, last year.

Northern also called for an end to uncertainty over whether the bid will be approved by the UK government as this has helped to dampen shares, which were trading at 610 pence by 1147 GMT, and called for the bid to be decided on value. ($1=.5994 Pound)
